The Social Worker
adopts a client-centred and strengths-based approach to support clients in achieving their rehabilitation goals, enhancing psychosocial well-being, and promoting independent living and community integration.

Responsibilities

1.    Client Assessment & Case Management

Conduct comprehensive intake assessments and interviews with clients, family members, and caregivers, including registration for SAVH services
Assess clients’ psychosocial, financial, family and support needs, and develop appropriate intervention plans
Develop, implement and review set goals with clients and relevant stakeholders measurable outcomes
Provide case management and follow-up services to support clients’ rehabilitation and adjustment to vision loss
Conduct home visits where required to better assess client’s living conditions and support needs
Maintain accurate, timely, and comprehensive case records, case notes, assessments, and related documentation in accordance with organisational policies and professional standards

Collaborate and participate in case discussion with internal departments and multidisciplinary teams to ensure coordinated and client-centred service delivery
Liaise with healthcare institutions, social service agencies and community partners on referrals, rehabilitation, and support services
Work with relevant stakeholders to facilitate clients’ access to appropriate community resources, financial assistance and social support
Support the coordination and utilisation of Low Vision Devices (LVDs) through the Assistive Device Centre (ADC), including facilitating communication among clients, healthcare providers, and relevant stakeholders.
Encourage and support client participation in the Vision Rehabilitation Programme (VRP) to promote engagement and rehabilitation outcomes

3.    Counselling and Intervention

Provide counselling, emotional support, appropriate psychosocial interventions to clients and their families
Support clients in adjusting to vision loss and developing coping strategies, resilience and self-advocacy skills
Provide support in areas such as family relationships, financial difficulties, social isolation, emotional well-being and independent living
Identify and respond appropriately to clients who may require additional or specialised support, including making referrals to relevant services where appropriate
Support clients and families during period of crisis or significant life transitions, with appropriate consultation and supervision where required

4.    Community Engagement & Programme Development

Participate in outreach, engagement, and Association events to increase awareness of Association’s services available to persons with visual impairment
Contribute to and support community initiatives that promote inclusion, accessibility and participation of persons with visual impairment
Gather feedback from clients and stakeholders to identify service needs and opportunities for improvement

5.    Monitoring, Reporting & Professional Practice

Monitor and evaluate client progress against intervention goals
Prepare case reports, programme statistics and other documentation required for service monitoring, evaluation, and funding requirements, including submissions via the EPES system
Participate actively in case discussions, team meetings, supervision, training, and professional development to enhance service delivery and maintain professional competency
Maintain professional boundaries, confidentiality and ethical standards in all aspects of practice
Keep abreast of relevant developments in social work practice, disability services and rehabilitation

Promote a culture of learning and continuous improvement by sharing relevant knowledge, best practices, research insights, and new approaches with the team
Undertake additional duties and responsibilities as assigned by the Head of Department (HOD)

About the Position 

We are looking for a Supportive Housing Peer Support Specialist
(PSS) to join our team at our Rogue Ridge Apartments in Ashland, Oregon! ColumbiaCare Services is looking for the right individual to work Peer-to-Peer, meaning you have personal experience with mental health challenges and are a recipient of mental health services, and are willing to share your experiences with adult mental health consumers. The Supportive Housing Peer Support Specialist meets with each new resident to support the individual in feeling welcome, answer questions, and provide compassionate support and guidance in setting self-determined goals. The Supportive Housing Peer Support Specialist will engage with residents one-on-one as well as coordinate and facilitate peer groups, provide personal care services (including shopping, self-help, socialization, meal preparation, and more), and utilize strategic self-disclosure with residents to build connection and normalize mental health challenges.

About the Program

Rogue Ridge is 26-unit Permanent Supportive Housing program providing affordable housing to local citizens who are low-income and chronically without housing, along with a combination of behavioral health and tenancy supports.

General staffing includes an on-site Resident Manager available to provide access to housing support; and a Supportive Housing Associate and Certified Recovery Mentor (Peer) providing 7-day a week presence and services such as skills training, tenancy assistance, housing stabilization, and community navigation. The program is supervised by a full-time Supportive Housing Supervisor, and ColumbiaCare's Property Management team offers tenancy support around move in/out, rent collection, and maintenance and repairs.

talk, listen, use hands and fingers, reach, stand, walk, sit, bend, stoop, climb stairs, as well as lift, carry, push, and pull up to 40 pounds

use ladders, squat/kneel, and perform other physical tasks as applicable. In addition, you must successfully complete crisis de-escalation and CPR trainings, which require performing various physical, hands-on maneuvers and techniques and may require an individual to lift and transfer clients.

new_jobs.title: Case Manager - Day Report Center - Waukesha
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary:
This position provides intensive case management, supervision, and support to three referral sources: The program serves individuals Court ordered to the Day Report Center, an alternative to incarceration, individuals that enter into a  Deferred Prosecution agreement with the District Attorney’s Office, as either a standard Diversion or a Pre-charge Diversion agreement, as well as to those individuals referred by the Department of Correction Probation Agents.  It requires a bachelor’s degree, and Case Managers must follow the national diversion standards as published by the National Association of Pretrial Services Agencies (Diversion). The Case Managers follow results of evidence-based assessments, including GAIN and RANT, which guide their decisions to determine level of risk and need for eligibility and support provided by the program.  Case Managers receive specialized training and receive certification in conducting the Level of Service Case Management Inventory (LS-CMI), which guides them in developing case plans that address individuals’ criminogenic risk and needs. Case Managers also receive specialized training in evidence-based curriculums, including Thinking for a Change and Carey Guides and Brief Intervention Tools (BITS).  While providing supervision and support, the Case Managers must make independent decisions and provide resources to meet the needs of people served. Case Managers must produce compliance reports to the Courts, which are relied upon for recommendations for sanctions, and communicate directly with the DA’s Office and Probation Agents to help determine their response to violations. Case Manager’s work independently in monitoring compliance, writing court letters, making referrals to treatment and treatment provider updates, and independently develop and produce recommendations for violations. Case Managers have contact with people served, court officials and stakeholders, treatment providers, probation agents, community-based organizations, attorneys, and individuals identified on Releases of Information, and other WCS staff and leadership.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
•    Responsible for a range of evidence-based services to provide structure and accountability, including but not limited to: conducting the LS-CMI Assessment and analyzing all required assessments prior to admission and intake and developing case plans for persons served; facilitating new intakes and explaining the program components to persons served, face-to-face supervision appointments with people to support compliance with all program requirements and terms of supervision, identify and provide people with community based services for supportive services based on need, as well as conduct skill building activities during supervision appointments, facilitate evidence-based curriculum, including Thinking for a change and Carey Guides, BITS, routine alcohol and drug testing, working with local treatment providers to ensure enrollment in and compliance with treatment, and support people with compliance with all related fees (program, court, treatment, and electronic monitoring).
•    Engage in internal team meetings and use professional judgement to make recommendations for responses to violations.
•    Using professional judgement to make independent decisions for treatment provider referrals based on people’s needs and support and ensure accountability and compliance with provider standards.
•    Ensure that the national standards for diversion programs supervision model and its core elements are followed, including use of the assigned assessment tools.
•    Enter appropriate tracking in the WCS AWARDS and CORE databases, ensuring timely and complete data entry.
•    Provide court testimony as requested.
•    Conduct, monitor and evaluate drug and alcohol testing in the Waukesha Court Services programs, ensuring the integrity of all alcohol and drug testing procedures, and report results to the Court and all parties. 
•    Make independent recommendations to the Court, District Attorney’s Office, and the Department of Corrections- Agents for response to violations.
•    Ensure accurate and timely written and electronic files and court communication.
•    Coordinate with the Electronic Monitoring services and staff and ensure routine check ins for inspection of the bracelet, and payment of fees, including addressing outstanding fees owed by people served.
•    Attend the Waukesha County Victim Impact Panel at least once per year.
•    Other job-related duties may be necessary to carry out the responsibilities of the position

Required Qualifications
•    Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, Social Work or other related field; experience in working with individuals experiencing mental health and/or substance use disorders.
•    Prior experience in a case management role and ability to function independently and work as a team.
•    Experience working with Community Based Organizations, and referrals and follow up to meet the needs of people served.
•    Ability to work collaboratively with justice system stakeholders including judges, attorneys, jail staff, probation agents, treatment providers, and other partners.
•    Possess a valid Wisconsin Driver’s License and maintain adequate auto.
•    Must pass driver’s license check, employment drug test and background checks.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
•    Communication – strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to provide information effectively with a diverse population - the persons we serve, supervisor, colleagues, judges, District Attorney, Department of Corrections Probation Agents, in writing and oral communications.
•    Technological Aptitude – Ability to use general technological skills throughout daily job i.e., Email, Internet, company specified systems, (ex. Microsoft 365, Windows, Word, Excel).
•    Managing Priorities/Deadlines – Ability to organize and maintain schedules, meet deadlines and manage multiple projects.
•    Problem-Solving Skills – Ability to think critically, operate independently, and be solution-oriented in a fast-paced environment and adapt to program changes and challenges, including crisis situations.
•    Adaptability – Ability to manage change, deal with situations as they arise and work independently or as part of a team.
•    Teamwork – Ability to work productively as a team while also managing independent duties and responsibilities.
•    Motivation – Possess a commitment to the assigned job, mission and core values of the organization while also supporting a respectful and harmonious work setting.
•    Professionalism – Ability to conduct oneself with a high level of integrity, ethics and boundaries. Maintain professional and respectful communication with coworkers, people served, and all external people and agencies involved with service provision.
•    Multicultural Sensitivity – The role involves working and interacting directly with diverse populations, including people served, partners, and service providers. As such, the employee must demonstrate professionalism, cultural sensitivity, and strong interpersonal skills while representing the organization in a variety of settings.
•    Knowledge of Evidence-Based Principles, including Motivational Interviewing, Trauma-Informed Care, Person-centered care, and other funder and agency adopted principles, as well as following models for fidelity established by the agency. Complete training in all agency-required EBP’s within six months of hire unless otherwise directed by the Assistant Program Manager and Director of Waukesha Court Services.
•    Follow the Agency Code of Conduct, provided at agency employment and program orientation.
•    Program Specific Knowledge, Skills and Abilities – Knowledge of National Pretrial and Diversion Standards and best practices within post-conviction and diversion programs, familiarity with the Wisconsin Justice System; knowledge community resources to include housing, education, public transportation; knowledge of the Wisconsin Circuit Court Access Program (CCAP).

PM21

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
Duties require good hearing and the ability to communicate verbally; hand and finger dexterity for data entry and typing; involves very minimal driving in Waukesha County and requires some direct observation drug testing. 
WORK ENVIRONMENT:
Work is performed primarily in an office setting but also includes going to court occasionally, and rarely in other locations. The employee also is responsible for conducting, observing/supervising, and evaluation of results for drug screens of people in programs. People served may exhibit disruptive behavior at times. The position is full-time, 40 hours each week to include periodic assigned Saturdays (7:00-10:00am) for drug and alcohol testing. The employee has contact with a wide variety of individuals to include justice-involved individuals, court officials, law enforcement, jail staff, treatment and other services providers, DOC staff, other justice agencies, other WCS staff, and family members of individuals served.
